Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (p.75, matching seed_citation context 'p.75') lists 'Intesar/Sahel | Sirte Oil | 80 [mi] | 30 [in] | 19,824,412 [1,000 scm/yr] | na' — an existing, catalogued gas pipeline with a stated capacity as of 2011 data, i.e. operating at that point. Separately, 2026 reporting (Libya Herald, and consistent with Ecofin/Libya Observer/attaqa.net, all independently verified) describes a NEW parallel 42-inch pipeline (Zueitina Field 103 to Sirte Oil's Line 36B, ~130 km) completing trial operation in April 2026 after being 'halted before 2011' — built specifically to relieve back-pressure/flaring on the existing Intisar-Irada-Sahel-Brega gas corridor. This confirms that corridor (which includes this 30in Intesar/Sahel segment) remained an active, in-service gas system as of 2026, not shelved or decommissioned. No source states the 30in Intesar/Sahel segment itself was taken offline or replaced — the 42in line is additional capacity, not a replacement. Medium tier: OPEC source is a strong direct table entry; 2026 status support is corridor-level context/inference rather than a direct statement naming this specific 30in segment, per the protocol's status-is-inferable guidance.

OPEC ASB2012 lists the Intesar/Sahel line under 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (Table 4.10), directly confirming Fuel=Gas. Libya Herald 2026 independently confirms the same corridor (Zueitina Field 103/Sirte Line 36B/Brega network) is a gas transport system. Two independent sources agree; trivial/uncontested fact.

OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 (p.75): 'Intesar/Sahel | Sirte Oil | 80 | 30 | 19,824,412 | na', column header 'Capacity (1,000 scm/yr)'. 19,824,412 thousand scm/yr = 19,824,412,000 scm/yr = 19.824 bcm/y, matching GEM's Capacity=19.82 (rounded) almost exactly. Note: this is distinct from the 2026 news figure of '~150 million cubic feet/day of previously-flared gas recovered' by the NEW 42in parallel pipeline (Zueitina Field 103/Line 36B) — that figure describes recovered/incremental flared-gas volume on the new line, not this pipeline's nameplate capacity, and should not be confused with or substituted for the OPEC capacity value. Single strong source found for the exact figure; no second independent source with this granularity located despite searching Sirte Oil/NOC/MEED/academic sources.

OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 (p.75), column header 'Length (miles)': Intesar/Sahel = 80 miles = ~128.7 km, matching GEM's LengthKnown=129.00 km. Note the co-located 'Sahel/km-81.5 | Sirte Oil | 49 | 30 | 19,541,206' row in the same table is a DIFFERENT, shorter downstream segment — not to be confused with this Intesar-to-Sahel segment. Single strong source; no independent second source with this exact mileage found.

OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 (p.75), column 'Diameter (inches)': Intesar/Sahel = 30, matching GEM's Diameter=30.00 in exactly. IMPORTANT — do not conflate with the 42-inch pipeline widely reported in April 2026 news (Libya Herald, Ecofin, Libya Observer, Pipeline Technology Journal, PGJ, attaqa.net, all independently verified): that is a separate, newly-completed parallel line (Zueitina Field 103 to Sirte Oil's Line 36B, a project 'halted before 2011' and finished in 2026), not this pre-existing 30in Intesar/Sahel segment. The two coexist in the same corridor. Single strong source for the 30in figure on THIS specific segment; no second independent source with this granularity found.

OPEC ASB2012 lists this line under its 'Libya' country section (Sirte Basin, Sirte Oil-operated network). Libya Herald 2026 independently confirms the Intisar/Zueitina Field 103-Sahel-Brega corridor sits in Libya's Sirte Basin. Both StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea=Libya are trivially and independently corroborated.

OPEC ASB2012 names the direct operator of the Intesar/Sahel line as 'Sirte Oil' (not literally 'Libyan National Oil Corp'). Wikipedia's Sirte Oil Company entry independently states 'Sirte Oil Company (SOC) is an oil and gas company in Libya operating under the state-owned National Oil Corporation (NOC)' and that SOC 'was formed as a NOC subsidiary.' Together these support GEM's Owner1=Libyan National Oil Corp/100% as the ultimate state parent owner, with Sirte Oil as the operating subsidiary — consistent with how GEM typically records ultimate ownership of Libyan state oil/gas infrastructure. Neither single source states 'NOC' as literal operator of this exact segment, so this is an inference chain (parent-subsidiary) rather than a direct value-present match; tier medium.
